summary: New box Infinitiv: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (113/34)

data.turoyo: W bəṯr disane komər maḥatle iḏo bu gwoyo w gwele.
data.translation: Danach Streckte er wieder die Hand zum Betteln aus und bettelte.

rationale: New I Infinitiv box; gwoyo is already embedded in the Preterit quotation, now illustrated under its own form without changing meaning.

data.turoyo: tə=mede latte w i=emo ggawyo w kobole koxəl.
data.translation: sie hatten gar nichts; die Mutter bettelte und gab ihm zu essen.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; feminine subject, begging as livelihood.

data.turoyo: Harke bayn i ʕaširayḏi ste lo kowe, d goweno. Lazəm yo eli, d qoyamno annaqqa, əzzino bi arʕo.
data.translation: Hier im Stamm kann ich nicht Betteln gehen. Ich muß mich aufmachen und in die weite Welt gehen.

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; first-person bare form and explicit social/location restriction.

summary: All eight tokens retain inherited betteln. Bare, g-/ko-prefixed and feminine/plural-looking orthographic variants are contextual forms of the same I Infectum; no second stem is supported.
Beggar is the sole overt argument, with food or requested goods implicit. The corpus adds a feminine breadwinner and a first-person social restriction on begging, rather than a lexical distinction.

maḥatle iḏo bu gwoyo names extending the hand for begging; the supplied verse may describe a literal gesture. It does not establish a separate light-verb sense. The nominal gwoyo warrants an Infinitiv box despite being embedded in an existing example.
Confirm whether maḥatle iḏo bu gwoyo is conventional for taking up begging or describes a literal outstretched-hand gesture. No new idiom is asserted from that ambiguity.
